jsonld.name: Mafroum Stuffed Potatoes
jsonld.description: Mafroum is the Libyan Sephardic kitchen's tour de force: thick potato slices hollowed and stuffed with spiced meat, sealed, breaded, fried, and finally simmered gently in a light lemon-onion sauce — one vegetable, one meat, and five techniques in a single dish. It is the Sabbath table's own labor of love in Tripoli's former community, the dish whose making filled the Friday kitchen and whose serving crowned it. The craft is the hollowing and the seal; the pot's patience finishes what the fry began.

skeleton:
Mafroum Stuffed Potatoes

Libyan · Hard · Makes about 12 mafroum (serves 4–6)

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
Mafroum is the Libyan Sephardic kitchen's tour de force: thick potato slices hollowed and stuffed with spiced meat, sealed, breaded, fried, and finally simmered gently in a light lemon-onion sauce — one vegetable, one meat, and five techniques in a single dish. It is the Sabbath table's own labor of love in Tripoli's former community, the dish whose making filled the Friday kitchen and whose serving crowned it. The craft is the hollowing and the seal; the pot's patience finishes what the fry began.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

The potatoes and the filling

  • 12 to 14 slices

The breading and the fry

The sauce and the simmer

- **Hollow with the melon-baller's patience — the walls run a centimeter.** Each potato slice's center scooped to a shell, the saved flesh reserved for another pot; the shell's walls must hold through the stuffing, the fry, and the simmer's gentleness. The shells soaked in cold water until their moment (the potato's brown, the artichoke's law). - **The seal's law:** the stuffed mafroum closes with a second thin potato slice or its own scooped lid, pressed firmly — the meat fully enclosed before the flour-egg-crumb, because an open edge leaks into the oil and the fry's whole architecture fails. The breading is the seal's second wall.

Doneness & Quality Checkpoints

  • The hollow: centimeter walls, the shells water-held until stuffed.
  • The seal: closed, pressed, breading's full coat — no meat's escape.
  • The simmer: the fork's silk, the meat's just-cooked, the lemon through both.

Mafroum Stuffed Potatoes

Prep: 1 hour · Cook: 1 hour · Total: About 2 hours · Makes about 12 mafroum (serves 4–6)

Ingredients

The potatoes and the filling

  • 6 large starchy potatoes (about 1.5 kg), peeled, cut crosswise to 3 cm slices — 12 to 14 slices
  • 400 g ground beef or lamb; 1 onion (about 150 g), grated; 3 cloves garlic (about 12 g), grated
  • A fist of parsley (about 20 g), minced; 1 tsp cumin; ½ tsp cinnamon; ½ tsp allspice; ½ tsp chile flakes; 1 tsp salt; black pepper
  • 1 egg (about 50 g), beaten, half into the meat and half for the breading

The breading and the fry

  • 60 g flour; 1 egg, beaten; 100 g fine dried breadcrumbs or matza meal (the Passover truth)
  • Neutral oil, 2 cm deep, at 175 °C

The sauce and the simmer

  • 3 tbsp olive oil (about 40 g); 2 onions (about 300 g), sliced thin
  • 2 cloves garlic, sliced; the juice of 1½ lemons (about 45 ml); 1 tsp salt; ½ tsp sugar
  • 400 ml water or light stock (about 400 g); a fist of cilantro (about 15 g)

Instructions

  1. **Make the filling, stuff, and seal (40 minutes).** Mix the meat with the grated onion, garlic, herbs, spices, half the beaten egg, and the salt — kneaded 3 minutes to a bound paste. Pat the shells dry; fill each with a rounded spoonful of the meat, and close: a thin slice of the reserved potato laid over and pressed, or the shell's own scooped lid. Rest the filled shells 15 minutes in the refrigerator (the seal's firming). Checkpoint — each filled mafroum: closed, firm, and no meat visible at the seam — the seal's proof at the press. The meat's mound must sit flush or below the shell's rim (an over-stuffed mafroum bursts at the fry).
  2. **Bread and fry (4 minutes a batch).** Flour, then egg, then crumbs — each mafroum pressed gently in the crumb to a full coat — and fried at 175 °C to a deep gold, turning once, in small batches. Drain briefly. Checkpoint — the fry's target: a closed, golden crust — the mafroum set in its breading's armor, the meat within only begun (the simmer finishes it). A burst mafroum in the oil was an open seam — the next batch's seal doubled.
  3. **The sauce's simmer (45 minutes at the gentlest tremble).** Soften the sliced onions in the olive oil 8 minutes to a golden silk; the garlic 1 minute more; the lemon juice, the salt, the sugar, and the water — the fried mafroum nestled in the sauce in one layer, covered, and trembled (barely 90 °C) 40 to 45 minutes, spooning the sauce over twice, until the potatoes are fork-silk through and the meat's center runs cooked and juicy. Checkpoint — a mafroum's test at the 40th minute: pierce the potato's wall at its thickest — the fork runs through with no resistance, and the meat's center reads just-cooked and moist (the fry's crust has given its body to the sauce, and the sauce's lemon has run through the meat). The sauce itself: a light, lemony gold-silk — the onions dissolved to a thickened body — spooned generously over each serving.
  4. **The service.** The pot to the table: each mafroum lifted whole (a spatula's mercy — the silk potato's fragility), the sauce ladled over, the cilantro scattered. Checkpoint — eating test: the potato's silk — the simmer's whole patience, barely holding its shape at the spoon — giving to the meatball's savory-spiced center (the cinnamon-allspice register unmistakable), the lemon sauce running through both, and the crust's faint memory at the edge. It should taste like the Friday kitchen's own argument: the labor that love pays forward, and the pot's patience that finishes it.

Finish & Plate

Each mafroum lifted whole to the plate — the silk potato's gold under the lemon sauce's shine, the cilantro's green over — a wet spoon beside the dry, and the table's own care the dish's final service.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Mafroum burst at the fryOpen seam or over-stuffedThe flush seal, doubled at the press
Potato still firm at 45 minutesSimmer boiled, not trembledThe 90 °C gentleness — the fry set it; only time softens
Sauce sharp past pleasureLemon over-runThe sugar's pinch balances — taste at the 20th

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- The stuffed, breaded, un-fried mafroum freeze 1 month (fry and simmer from frozen, +10 minutes); the cooked pot keeps 2 days and re-trembles gently. The filling batch keeps 2 days for the next hollowing. - Variations: the zucchini's summer cousin (a shorter clock), the onion-shell register. The #62 is the Sephardic block's stuffed craft; the #54 osban runs the casing's own row on this site.
